summary: Okanogan National Forest summit: a pole platform tower and cabin dated only to the 1930s, now gone; the climb today is a long off-trail route from Wolf Creek.

facts.design: Pole platform tower; the register also describes a cabin, which Willhite calls only possible
facts.status_note: The register and FireLookout.com say the pole platform tower and cabin are gone; no source describes what remains.

access.note: Inside the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness, per Willhite. The route starts at the Wolf Creek Trailhead and leaves the trail for the summit.

visit.trail_note: Nothing to climb. Willhite's route runs about 10 miles up the Wolf Creek Trail to Gardner Meadows, then an off-trail climb.

events.note: Registered November 17, 2012 as US 1447, WA 347; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com both say the 1930s, and Willhite gives the same decade without a year. No source gives a single year, so no built event is recorded.
The register describes a cabin that stood there; Willhite says a cabin was only possible. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three short pages, with no year finer than the 1930s, and no independent record found (one search added nothing). Willhite says DNR records show the site, while the register lists the U.S. Forest Service as administrator; the story does not resolve which agency held it. The brief's coordinates (48.50709, -120.48816) and elevation (2711.8 m) match the register (N 48.507090, W 120.488160; 2,712 m), so no corrections. Access 'public' rests on Willhite's route description in a wilderness area; check current wilderness rules before publishing. Read budget: six fetches, two of which were lookout lists that added nothing.
